bands.1:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Comma Cay. Snow is falling. A white mountain curls over at the top like a giant comma.

"There is an 81 per cent chance my nose has frozen off," says Tully.

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak. The water freezes into a tiny ice rink.

Stashlets bury seeds in neat rows. A Dotumble is curled up in a ball. It looks like a full stop in the snow.

"Hello," Zed says to a Quotoo.

"Hello," says the Quotoo, in Zed's voice.

At the top of a gold chairlift is a gold lodge. The sign says, "MAXX'S SNOW RESCUE LODGE. NO QUESTIONS."

"Who hates questions?" asks Indi.

"Maxx does," says Wren.

A tall skier zooms down. She has silver hair and a very long scarf. A little red robin sits on her ski pole.

"Welcome, comma, strangers, full stop," she says. "I am Madame Pause, full stop."

"She says the punctuation!" whispers Zed.

Mo is hungry. "Let's eat Madame Pause!"

"Let's eat, COMMA, Madame Pause!" she snaps. "With no comma, I am the lunch, full stop."

Zed starts to explain. "We think Maxx is stealing Creatures and we have a map and we want to..."

Peck! The robin pecks his nose.

"That is Stoppit, full stop," says Madame Pause. "Stoppit hates sentences that never end, full stop."

Her Creatures keep going missing. She asked Maxx where they went. Her question was deleted in one second.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge, comma, Captain, full stop." She skis away.

That night, Indi types a comment for Maxx. "Is the possum scared?"

It vanishes. A gold message pops up. "No questions on Comma Cay, Captain. Stay gold."

Up on the mountain, a hundred red eyes blink on.
bands.2:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Comma Cay through swirling snow. The island has one white mountain that curls over at the top, just like a giant comma.

"Statistically," says Tully, through chattering teeth, "there is an 81 per cent chance my nose has frozen off."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak, and the water freezes into a tiny ice rink on the deck.

The snow is full of Creatures. Stashlets bury seeds in neat rows. A Dotumble has curled into a ball so round that it looks like a full stop dropped in the snow.

"Hello," Zed says to a Quotoo in a snow gum.

"Hello," says the Quotoo, in Zed's exact voice.

"Why did the snowman call his dog Frost?" asks Mo. "Because Frost bites!"

"Frost bites," repeats the Quotoo. Then it groans.

At the top of a gold chairlift stands a gold glass lodge. Its sign says, "MAXX'S SNOW RESCUE LODGE. NO QUESTIONS."

"Who builds a rescue lodge with no questions?" asks Indi.

"Someone who can't stand them," says Wren. She pulls her beanie down.

A tall skier swoops down beside the boat. She has silver hair and a scarf so long that it trails behind her. A small round robin with a red chest sits on her ski pole.

"Welcome, comma, strangers, full stop," she says. "I am Madame Pause, comma, Keeper of Comma Cay, full stop."

"Did she just say the punctuation out loud?" whispers Zed.

Mo rubs his hands together. "Great! Let's eat Madame Pause!"

Her eyebrows shoot up. "Let's eat, COMMA, Madame Pause! Without the comma, I am not your guest. I am your lunch, full stop."

Zed tries to explain. "We think Maxx is stealing Creatures and we have a map and we want to..."

The robin hops onto his head and pecks his nose.

"Ow!"

"That is Stoppit, full stop," says Madame Pause. "Stoppit cannot bear a sentence that never ends, full stop."

Then she grows serious. Since Maxx arrived, her Creatures have been vanishing. She asked Maxx where they were going, in a comment under his stream. It was deleted in one second. So was every question after it.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge, comma, Captain, full stop," she says. Then she skis away.

That night, Indi types a comment under Maxx's live stream: "Is the possum in your video scared?"

It disappears. A new message pops up in gold letters: "No questions on Comma Cay, Captain. Stay gold."

Up on the mountain, every light in the lodge swings round to face your boat. Behind the glass, a hundred tiny red eyes blink on.
bands.3:
The Soggy Biscuit noses into Comma Cay through a flurry of snow, its deck already crunchy with ice. The island is small and steep, with a single white mountain that curls over at the top like a giant comma.

"Statistically," says Tully, through chattering teeth, "there is an 81 per cent chance that my nose has frozen off. I can't check, because my fingers have frozen off too."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak, and the water freezes instantly into a tiny ice rink.

The snow is alive with Creatures, once you know where to look. A row of Stashlets is burying seeds in perfect lines, with a neat gap between each one. A Dotumble has curled itself into a ball so round that it looks like a full stop someone dropped in the snow. In a snow gum, a Quotoo with a red crest tilts its head at you.

"Hello," says Zed.

"Hello," says the Quotoo, in Zed's exact voice.

"Why did the snowman call his dog Frost?" asks Mo. "Because Frost bites!"

"Because Frost bites," repeats the Quotoo, and then it groans, which is somehow worse.

Mo's lunch is frozen prawn icy poles. Gus calls them "a fascinating experiment", which is the nicest thing anyone says.

Halfway up the mountain, at the top of a shining gold chairlift, sits a lodge made of gold glass. Its sign says, "MAXX'S SNOW RESCUE LODGE. NO QUESTIONS."

Indi squints. "Who builds a rescue lodge that doesn't allow questions?"

"Someone who can't stand them," Wren says flatly. She tugs her beanie down over her eyes.

A skier swoops down the slope and stops beside the boat in a spray of snow. She is tall and silver-haired, with a scarf so long that it trails behind her like a tail. A small round robin with a red chest perches on her ski pole.

"Welcome, comma, strangers, full stop," she says. "I am Madame Pause, comma, Keeper of Comma Cay, full stop."

Zed blinks. "Did she just say the punctuation out loud?"

"Every mark matters, full stop," says Madame Pause.

Mo, who is very hungry, rubs his hands together. "Great! Let's eat Madame Pause!"

Her eyebrows shoot up into her hair. "Let's eat, COMMA, Madame Pause! One little comma is the difference between inviting me to lunch and having me FOR lunch, full stop."

Zed tries to explain. "We're here because Maxx is stealing Creatures and we've got a map and we think his base is in that lodge and we want to..."

The robin hops onto his head and pecks him smartly on the nose.

"Ow!"

"That is Stoppit, full stop," says Madame Pause. "Stoppit cannot bear a sentence that never ends, full stop. Neither can I, full stop."

Then her face grows serious. Since Maxx arrived, her Creatures have been vanishing from the slopes. So she asked him where they were going, in a comment under his stream. It vanished in under a second. She asked a hundred times. Every question was deleted.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

She studies you over her scarf. "Win my badge, comma, Captain, full stop. Until then, comma, stay off my slopes, full stop." She pushes off and is gone.

That evening, Indi types a comment under Maxx's live stream: "Is the possum in your video scared?"

The comment blinks once. Then it disappears. A new message pops up in shiny gold letters: "No questions on Comma Cay, Captain. Stay gold."

Up on the mountain, every light in the gold lodge swings round to face the Soggy Biscuit. Behind the glass, a hundred tiny red eyes blink on at once.
bands.4:
The Soggy Biscuit noses into Comma Cay through a flurry of snow, its deck already crunchy with ice. The island is small and steep, with a single white mountain that curls over at the top like a giant comma. Everyone is wearing every jumper on board, and Gus is wearing two of Mo's as well.

"Statistically," says Tully, through chattering teeth, "there is an 81 per cent chance that my nose has frozen off. I can't check, because my fingers have frozen off too."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak, as it always does, and the water freezes instantly into a tiny ice rink. Zed skids across it twice before anyone can warn him.

The snow is alive with Creatures, once you know where to look. A row of Stashlets is burying seeds in perfect lines, with a neat gap between each one so they never roll together. A Dotumble has curled itself into a ball so round that it looks like a full stop someone dropped in the snow. In a twisted snow gum, a Quotoo with a scarlet crest tilts its head at you.

"Hello," says Zed.

"Hello," says the Quotoo, in Zed's exact voice.

"Why did the snowman call his dog Frost?" asks Mo. "Because Frost bites!"

"Because Frost bites," repeats the Quotoo, and then it groans, which is somehow worse than when the crew does it.

Mo's lunch is frozen prawn icy poles. Gus describes them as "a fascinating experiment in shrimp preservation", which is as close as anyone comes to a compliment.

Halfway up the mountain, at the top of a gleaming gold chairlift, sits a lodge made entirely of gold glass. Its sign is lit by a hundred little bulbs: "MAXX'S SNOW RESCUE LODGE. NO QUESTIONS." On the roof, a satellite dish the size of a swimming pool hums to itself.

Indi squints at it. "Who builds a rescue lodge that doesn't allow questions?"

"Someone who can't stand them," Wren says flatly. She tugs her beanie down over her eyes.

Before anyone can say a word, a skier swoops down the slope and stops right beside the boat in a glittering spray of snow. She is tall and silver-haired, with a scarf so long that it trails behind her like a tail. A small round robin with a red chest, as bright as a stop sign, perches on the tip of her ski pole.

"Welcome, comma, strangers, full stop," she says. "I am Madame Pause, comma, Keeper of Comma Cay, full stop."

Zed blinks. "Did she just say the punctuation out loud?"

"Every mark matters, full stop," says Madame Pause. "Say them, comma, and you will never forget them, full stop."

Mo, who is very hungry, rubs his hands together. "Great! Let's eat Madame Pause!"

Her eyebrows shoot up into her hair. "Let's eat, COMMA, Madame Pause! One little comma is the difference between inviting me to lunch and having me FOR lunch, full stop."

"Sorry," says Mo. "Would you like a prawn icy pole?"

"Absolutely not, full stop."

Zed tries to explain. "We're here because Maxx is stealing Creatures and pretending to rescue them and we've got a map and we think his base is inside that lodge and we want to..."

The robin hops onto his head and pecks him smartly on the nose.

"Ow!"

"That is Stoppit, full stop," says Madame Pause. "Stoppit cannot bear a sentence that never ends, full stop. Neither can I, full stop."

Then her face grows serious. Since Maxx arrived, she tells you, her Creatures have been vanishing from the slopes, a few every night. So she did the sensible thing and asked him. She wrote, "Where are the Comma Cay Creatures going?" under his latest stream. It vanished in under a second. She wrote it again, and again, a hundred times over. Every single question was deleted.

"Every question, comma, gone, full stop," she says. "As if questions frighten him, full stop."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

She studies you over the top of her scarf. "You want my trust, comma, Captain? Win my badge, full stop. Until then, comma, stay off my slopes, full stop."

She pushes off and disappears in a swirl of white.

That evening, Indi borrows the cracked tablet and types a comment under Maxx's live stream: "Is the possum in your video scared?"

The comment blinks once. Then it disappears. A new message pops up in its place, in shiny gold letters: "No questions on Comma Cay, Captain. Stay gold."

Up on the mountain, every light in the gold lodge swings round to face the Soggy Biscuit. Behind the glass, a hundred tiny red eyes blink on at once.
